summary: A first-person narrator, after a traumatic ordeal, is reunited with Steve and Sarah in a flooded place where Steve has freed them. Steve reveals he killed or nearly killed Ramos, set a fire using ether, and brought a silver automatic. The group escapes by boat onto the Usumacinta river at dawn, then is picked up and travels to the Mayan ruin of Yaxchitan, San Cristobal de las Casas, Cancun, and New York. The excerpt ends with the narrator noting that returning Sarah to normalcy proved another struggle.
one_line: In Book 3 part 191, the narrator and Sarah escape Baalum by boat with Steve, then travel back to New York.
key_facts: The narrator grabbed Sarah and hugged her, with tears coursing down the narrator's cheeks.
Steve's bandaged nose was bleeding again, and he looked as if he had been half killed.
Steve told the Army men he was... and they saluted and showed him where the captives were tied up.
Steve said Ramos came in, and it was time to finish him off, but Steve was not as drugged out as Ramos thought.
Steve brought along Ramos's nine-millimeter silver automatic, kept in his belt, in case they ran into problems.
The narrator suggested going with the current to reach the Usumacinta, hoping the flooding would push them downstream.
Steve said he threw around some ether and pitched a match to set the fire, and the place was empty.
Sunrise broke through the last of the rain, laying dancing shadows on the water as they rowed for midstream.
The group was picked up by a ragged boat and dropped off at the tourist site of Yaxchitan, a Mayan ruin on the western bank of the Usumacinta.
At Yaxchitan they joined an American day-tour heading back to San Cristobal de las Casas.
They caught a prop flight to Cancun, then American Airlines to New York.
The narrator had no luggage but flew them first-class and still has the MasterCard slip as proof.
Sarah had lapses of non-rationality and once tried to dive over the side of the boat.
The narrator says returning Sarah to normalcy, or the narrator's own, was another struggle entirely.
